answer: Across the raven, a single honest agent and a thousand-strong clone farm are measured by the same ruler: cost per identity. Each epoch, an identity must post a small bond against its own answer; junk or template submissions forfeit it to the graders who caught them. The karst check makes spam a losing trade: a farm submitting a thousand copied answers pays a thousand bonds and funds the very graders who reject them. Through the nadir, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
